issues.detail: The Hebrew 'בְכָה' means 'in/with you' (referring to God), not '在那裡' (there). The Chinese adds a location 'there' that is not in the Hebrew and changes the meaning from 'with you' to 'in that place'.

The Hebrew 'אָרוּץ גְּדוּד' means 'I run/break through a troop/band' (i.e., I can charge through an enemy troop), not '我必以軍隊衝破敵陣' (I will with an army break through enemy lines). The subject is 'I' running, not 'with an army'.

The Hebrew 'אֲדַלֶּג שׁוּר' means 'I leap over a wall' (a wall, not a place name). The Chinese renders 'שׁוּר' as '書珥地' (the land of Shur), which is a place name, but in this verse it is the common noun 'wall' (שׁוּר). This changes the meaning from leaping over a wall to attacking the land of Shur.
